edition_title: September 2026: The Doors Open Before the Deadlines Do
edition_intro: Ambitious young Nigerians do not wait for permission, they track deadlines like appointments. This edition rounds up five live opportunities worth your time this month: a fully funded master's in Beijing, a nine-figure naira startup grant, free tech expo access in Lagos, a ₦2.2 million essay prize, and a free route to a Microsoft certification. Move on these before the windows close.

posts.title: Schwarzman Scholars 2027-2028
posts.summary: A fully funded one-year master's degree at Tsinghua University in Beijing, covering tuition, housing, travel, and a stipend, built for future global leaders under 30.
posts.eligibility: Bachelor's degree holders worldwide, generally aged 24 to 29; open to Nigerians and all nationalities; no GRE, GMAT, or Mandarin required

posts.title: NiYA Startup Pitch 2.0
posts.summary: Up to ₦100 million in non-dilutive funding for 100 Nigerian startups, plus mentorship and enterprise tools, through the federal government's youth platform.
posts.eligibility: Nigerian founders aged 18 to 35, with a startup that has at least two co-founders and a completed NiYA profile

posts.title: GITEX Nigeria 2026
posts.summary: Free registration for West Africa's largest tech expo and AI summit, putting young builders in the same room as global tech leaders and investors in Lagos.
posts.eligibility: Open to all; free visitor registration, no invitation required

posts.title: Nigerian Economic Summit (NES #32)
posts.summary: A two-day national dialogue on jobs and productivity in Abuja, putting young Nigerians in the same room as policymakers, investors, and business leaders shaping economic reform.
posts.eligibility: Open to the public via pre-registration; students, entrepreneurs, and young professionals attend alongside policymakers

posts.title: NCDMB National Undergraduate Essay Competition 2026
posts.summary: ₦2.2 million in cash prizes and laptops for the best essays on local content and manufacturing, from Nigeria's oil and gas content regulator.
posts.eligibility: 100 or 200 level students at Nigerian universities, polytechnics, or colleges of education
